To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DASs with limited CSI feedback can significantly improve the throughput of both SU-MIMO and especially MU-MIMO transmission.

the throughput of MU-MIMO transmission can be improved in comparison to SU MIMO, even under the practical constraints of LTE, and that the performance of MU MIMO can be further improved by exploiting channel correlation and gain differences in the CSI feedback.

DASs with SU-MIMO or MU-MIMO transmission are a promising technology for future cellular systems, and that a simple feedback algorithm that exploits the available temporal correlation can significantly reduce the CSI overhead in DASs, especially for MU-MIMO transmission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of cellular systems, namely DASs.
the performance analysis of distributed antenna systems with multiple transmission points.
the performance analysis of distributed MIMO systems, and with the design and evaluation of practical CSI quantization schemes for DASs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAS with SU-MIMO is a good solution for the near future, while MU-MIMO is an attractive solution in the longer term.

DAS is an effective way of dealing with the path loss and large scale fading in cellular systems, and that MU-MIMO is an effective way for dealing with the small-scale fading in cellular system, and the combination of DAS and MU-MIMO can be an effective way for achieving the high throughput of the next generation cellular system.

the use of distributed antennas in cellular systems is beneficial, and that the use of MU-MIMO transmission is even more beneficial than SU-MIMO, especially if imperfect CSI at the base station is taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DAS with MU-MIMO can be implemented in a practical way with a significant gain in cell capacity.
DASs are an attractive solution to improve cell capacity and that MU-MIMO transmission can be efficiently implemented with limited feedback.
MU-MIMO transmission in DASs can provide significant throughput gains over SU-MIMO, even in practical systems with limited feedback and imperfect CSI at the transmitter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

MU-MIMO transmission in DASs with limited feedback can be very efficient, even in the presence of imperfect channel state knowledge at the transmitter, and that the gains of MU-MIMO over SU-MIMO transmission are not diminished by the limited feedback constraints.
DASs with coherent transmission across multiple antennas can achieve significant throughput gains compared to conventional cellular networks, even when imperfect CSI is used.
MU-MIMO is a very promising transmission strategy for cellular systems with distributed antennas.
